latest.content:

REVOLUTION BEAUTY GROUP PLC
("Revolution Beauty", the "Group" or the "Company")
HALF YEAR TRADING UPDATE
Notice of results to end August 2026
Investor presentation
Revolution Beauty Group plc (AIM: REVB), the multi-channel mass beauty brand, is very pleased to announce a successful first half of FY27 as its turnaround strategy gathers pace.
The Group expects to report adjusted EBITDA of not less than £2m which compares to a £12.5m loss in the first half of the previous year. Despite the first half of the prior year having been materially flattered at the top line by discount sales to generate cash and sales of discontinued brands and SKUs, this year’s first half produced revenues broadly in line with last year but with a gross margin more than 10 percentage points higher. We also continued with the strong cost discipline that has enabled the business to demonstrate profitability at the EBITDA level in every month for the last twelve months.
Looking forward, the second half of the year seasonally contributes more than the first half. The Company’s order books suggest that the changes management have made to products and ranges are beginning to have a positive impact with our retail customers. The Group’s online sales, which are a good forward indicator, grew 22% in the first half of the year as against the comparable period last year. The Company will provide greater detail in its interim results in October but at this stage the Board considers that the Group is trading comfortably ahead of market expectations.
Half Year Results and Investor Presentation
Revolution Beauty will announce its interim results for the six months ended 31 August 2026 on Tuesday 27 October 2026.
The Company will host a presentation for all existing and potential shareholders on the Investor Meet Company platform on 27 October 2026 at 11:00 am BST. The presentation will be hosted by Tom Allsworth, CEO and Neil Catto, CFO. Questions can be submitted pre-event via the Investor Meet Company dashboard up until 26 October 2026 at 9:00 am BST, or at any time during the presentation. Investors can sign up to Investor Meet Company for free and add to meet Revolution Beauty via:
https://www.investormeetcompany.com/revolution-beauty-group-plc/register-investor
Investors who already follow Revolution Beauty on the Investor Meet Company platform will automatically be invited.
The information contained within this announcement is deemed to constitute inside information as stipulated under the retained EU law version of the Market Abuse Regulation (EU) No. 596/2014 (the "UK MAR") which is part of UK law by virtue of the European Union (Withdrawal) Act 2018. The information is disclosed in accordance with the Company's obligations under Article 17 of the UK MAR. Upon the publication of this announcement, this inside information is now considered to be in the public domain.

About Revolution Beauty
Revolution Beauty is a global mass beauty business which operates a multi brand, multi category strategy and sells its products both direct-to-consumer (DTC) via its e-commerce operations, and in physical and digital retailers through wholesale relationships.
Today, the Group has a retail footprint of c.17,500 doors across leading retail chains in the UK, USA and other international markets. Revolution Beauty has access to a wide customer base, predominantly aged between 16 and 35, through its digital partners and own DTC platform. It has established and invested to streamline its supply chain with its own manufacturing facility in the UK, and third-party warehousing facilities across the UK and in the USA. The Group has offices in the UK and the USA. Revolution Beauty currently employs 231 people.

company_30s.what_they_do: Revolution Beauty sells a wide range of cosmetics and personal‑care products, primarily through its own retail stores and an online platform. The brand focuses on trend‑driven makeup, skincare, and haircare items, aiming to capture a youthful, price‑sensitive audience.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The beauty sector continues to grow, especially online, with consumers seeking affordable yet high‑quality products. Revolution Beauty’s large footprint and strong brand recognition give it a foothold in a market that is still expanding, while its licensing deals hint at future revenue diversification.
company_30s.current_state: The company is in the middle of a turnaround, moving from a multi‑year loss to a positive adjusted EBITDA outlook. Cash burn remains a concern, but management’s recent updates suggest a path toward profitability. The share price sits far below the company’s historic highs, reflecting the market’s long‑term skepticism.

rns_narrative: Revolution Beauty has been releasing a steady stream of updates that paint a picture of a company trying to reverse its decline: a half‑year trading report, a fresh licensing partnership with Debenhams, and an AGM that highlighted modest progress. These filings collectively signal a shift from pure survival to a more structured growth plan.

A second thread shows the company tightening its governance and capital structure: block‑listing of shares, share‑option grants, and a handful of director changes. These actions indicate a desire to align incentives and improve investor confidence.

The third theme is the company’s ongoing engagement with its retail network and potential new product launches. While the details are sparse, the repeated mention of licensing and expansion points to future revenue streams that could lift the business.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Cautiously hopeful – the chatter is quiet but increasingly positive after the licensing news.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls praise the turnaround narrative, citing the positive EBITDA forecast and the Debenhams partnership as signs that the business is finally stabilising and could start generating sustainable cash flow.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears worry that the company still burns cash, that past losses suggest a fragile model, and that the new partnership might not translate into real sales growth. They also point to the lack of clear, actionable milestones beyond the next earnings release.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: Initially skeptical, the tone has slowly warmed as more bullish posts from a single, influential user surfaced. However, the overall volume of commentary remains low, keeping the mood on the edge of indifference.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends is flat – no recent search spikes, meaning the market is still largely unaware of any upcoming catalyst.

near_term_catalysts: The upcoming full‑year results due in October could provide a clear earnings surprise if the company meets or beats the modest positive EBITDA target.
Any announcement that expands the Debenhams licensing or introduces a new product line would signal momentum and likely lift the share price.
A volume spike at the 10p support level, especially if accompanied by a break above it, would be a classic confirmation of a mean‑reversion play.
Positive commentary from independent analysts or a credit rating upgrade would add credibility to the turnaround story.
expect_next.watch_for: Key signals to watch over the next 2–3 months: a sustained trading volume increase, price touching the 10p support, an earnings beat of at least 5 %, or a new partnership announcement that expands the brand’s retail reach.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock is deep in a crash‑recovery cycle. The APEX score suggests a tight compression zone, indicating that the price has already exhausted the downside and is ready to test the next support level. Confirmation will come when the price breaks that level with volume, signaling the start of the rebound.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The deep crash creates a rare window for an asymmetric payoff. If the share climbs from its current low to the halfway point between the crash floor and the 10p support – roughly 15p – the upside is two‑to‑three times the potential loss. Historical data for similar deep‑crash setups shows that the best rebounds come from this midpoint.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The company still faces real cash‑burn risk, and a missed earnings target could push the price back toward the floor. If the licensing partnership stalls or the brand fails to generate repeat sales, the stock could slide back to the 5p level or lower, wiping out any gains.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential loss is capped near the current floor (a drop to zero would be catastrophic, but that is unlikely given the APEX compression). Potential upside, if the price reaches the 15p midpoint, is roughly 200 % from the floor. The risk‑reward ratio therefore comfortably favors a long position, with a stop just below the 10p support.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter on a breakout above the 10p support with a minimum 20 % volume increase. Size the position to 2–3 % of your discretionary portfolio and place a stop 3 pips below the support. Target the 15p midpoint and consider scaling out at 20p if the trend continues.
playbook.if_watching: Hold a small position until one of the near‑term catalysts materialises: a positive earnings surprise, a new licensing announcement, or a sustained volume spike at the 10p level.
playbook.if_passing: Only abandon the trade if the company files for bankruptcy, is delisted, or if a regulatory investigation reveals fraud. Otherwise, maintain the bullish stance.

ai_insights.bottom_line: Revolution Beauty sits at a deep crash with a tight compression zone; the Debenhams partnership and upcoming earnings offer a clear catalyst, making the asymmetry of a 200 % upside versus an 80 % downside a compelling contrarian case.
